title: super light weight, be careful where you use it, might be tripping hazard
text:
super light weight, be careful where you use it, might be tripping hazard. This review is for the variegated rag rug in Artichoke, 2'x3'

I often start with the positives, but my negative is too important so I am starting with that:
--I am surprised how very lightweight this rug is. I think this could be a problem. I am concerned that it could be a tripping hazard. I would recommend a grip backing added to it, or use it in a spot where people and pets are not going to trip on it. So no fast traffic areas- you know- areas where people/pets pick up speed, or possibly pivot. It wont stay in place for that. Preferably not on slick floors. I tried a couple of spots in the house. One near a doorway that has old linoleum tiles, and it moved around too much. Then I moved it to a back hallway where the flooring is bare planks with some texture on them. It should work here. I still think it will be kicked up or tripped over.

--It is very subtle in color, depending on the lighting, the green barely pops out.

I included pics of the rug in a couple of spots, but here are some non rug use ideas for it:

Possible other uses:
-- It could be used for non rug purpose- perhaps as a wider table runner, table mat, mat to put under pet food bowls, as seat cover, as a spot for kitties to sleep on, as a cover for back of a chair or couch (to protect from oily heads), as a safe out of the way from tripping accent floor mat, crate mat (if dogs dont chew), as a cat litter catcher, as a window blind (put up a rod, by curtain clips, clip this to those, and now you have a funky blind). Roll it up length wise and use it as a door draft blocker. Toss it over a bench. Giant counter top oven mat?
